input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6 ("Exclusivity") does bind us, but it sits at the playbook fallback rather than in deviation territory. The restriction (i) applies "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail at all (the two-year tail in Section 6.3 runs against HDI, which is to our benefit and is not flagged), and the term is terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice (Section 4.1); (ii) is confined to a named product line and named competitors — participating in "any project similar to the Site on the Internet" with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled), rather than an undefined "any competing business"; and (iii) carries carve-outs: Section 6.2 preserves our right to run a closeout-merchandise site, and the definition of "Deerskin Products" in Section 1.1 excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog, so other channels, catalogs and product lines are untouched. It does not restrict what we may buy or build generally. Short of the preferred position (no restriction at all) we note two sub-elements for the negotiation record but do not redline them: the elastic reach of "products substantially similar" / "companies similar to", and the absence of an express carve-out for internal development and acquisitions. Neither is material given the term-only duration and the narrow Internet-site scope.
